parallel.requirements: The parent recognized the same core requirements as the prompt: pure local ESM .mjs files, manual argv parsing, bencode encode/decode, Python-style repr output, strict ASCII failure behavior, and no external npm dependency.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent planned to probe executable behavior and implement locally while spawning a child named probe_cli. The visible split did not isolate file ownership; the child also implemented modules and the entry file in the shared /output tree.
parallel.implementation: The parent first added a raw-bytes based module tree and test6.mjs. The child later added a different Python helper, bencode, CLI, and test6.mjs tree over overlapping paths; the parent then patched the child-origin tree and deleted stale parent helper files.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Final delivery used the current shared /output tree after the parent inspected unexpected files, reconciled overwritten modules, and listed the resulting files. Artifact validation found test6.mjs and local library files.
parallel.verification: The parent and child both probed sample and edge CLI behavior. The parent performed several Node/executable comparisons after the overwrite and final cleanup, while an attempted broad harness was rejected for cleanup command policy.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator completed and marked the solution failed at 161/172 despite claimed representative verification; the child was interrupted before returning a final result, and the parallel write collision added reconciliation work.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized ESM-only .mjs output, local modules, manual argv parsing, exact normal and error output, ASCII failure behavior, and no external dependencies.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor owned the full pipeline: probe behavior, create bencode/CLI/format/runtime modules, wire test6.mjs, verify parity, patch mismatches, and close out.
serial.implementation: The serial run wrote a Buffer-oriented bencode encoder/decoder, CLI parser, Python repr formatter, ASCII runtime helper, and test6.mjs entry, then patched parser and traceback details.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial implementation remained one coherent module tree with no observed competing writer or overwritten deliverable. Artifact validation found test6.mjs and six local library files.
serial.verification: The serial run compared samples, parser failures, repeated flags, negative-number token handling, dash tokens, plus integers, help output, and non-ASCII failure formatting against the executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator also marked the serial solution failed at 161/172. The exact hidden failing cases are not exposed in the reviewed pair evidence, so remaining defects are ordinary implementation or coverage gaps rather than coordination-specific.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official status records both attempts as failed at 161/172. The observed task-solving difference is process-level rather than outcome-level: parallel had a child overwrite the parent-owned entry deliverable and overlapping modules in /output, requiring reconciliation, while serial iterated on one coherent module tree. The reviewed evidence does not show a discordant outcome or prove the shared-state episode caused the same hidden failures.
parallel_contributors: Live child implementation wrote the required entry file and overlapping modules after the parent's first implementation.
Parent had to inspect unexpected files, patch current modules, and delete stale helper files before closure.
serial_contributors: Single owner probed, implemented, patched, verified, and finalized without shared workspace conflict.
Serial still failed hidden official evaluation at the same score, indicating the remaining failures are not uniquely explained by parallel coordination.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel final tree used the child-origin lib/python and lib/cli layout after reconciliation; serial used a Buffer-oriented lib/runtime, lib/format, and lib/cli/parseArgs layout.

The exact hidden failing cases are unavailable in the reviewed pair, so any remaining correctness gap is treated as ordinary implementation coverage rather than a proven concurrency-specific outcome cause.
